dietary NaCl level modifies the integrated responses of rat CT nerves to NaCl alone and mixed with amiloride.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary NaCl on the development of the taste system in rats and how the taste system adapts to different levels of dietary NaCl.
the influence of dietary salt on gustatory transduction in adult rats.
the effect of early and late exposure to NaCl on taste transduction mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rearing on basal or high NaCl diets modifies the CT nerve response in rats, and that this response can be reversed by changing the dietary NaCl content of the diet.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CT nerve is sensitive to dietary NaCl exposure and the degree of sensitivity is dependent on the timing and duration of the exposure period.
the degree of inhibition of NaCl taste is a function of the level of NaCl in the diet, the duration of exposure, and the age of exposure.

rats reared on high NaCl diets demonstrate an increase in amiloride inhibition and a reduction in NaCl responsiveness, and rats reared on intermediate NaCl diets demonstrate a decrease in amiloride sensitivity and an increase in NaCl responsiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CT nerve response is modified by exposure to dietary NaCl and the degree of modification is dependent on the timing of the exposure.
there is a critical period for dietary NaCl exposure during development that is important for the development of the amiloride inhibition mechanism.
the CT nerve is a useful biomarker of NaCl intake in rats and may be useful for monitoring the effects of dietary NaCl on the taste system in other species.
